note: An instructive inversion of the stated ICP. On the physical criteria he is close to ideal: 34, 62.5 kg at 167 cm, ten unbroken years of training, a marathon completed, and a plateau he wants broken rather than a rescue he needs — "I sort of hit a plateau with how much weight I lift... I don't feel pumped at all." That is good-to-great in the ICP's own words, and nothing about him resembles the excluded profile. On the commercial criteria he misses all three. He is a salaried IT employee rather than a business owner or physician, and wants out of it entirely — "I would like to switch jobs and do something more physical." Income fails on the numbers the rep himself established: $3,000 in savings, roughly $200 a month left after bills, no credit card and no investments, against a $6,000 price he called "a bit higher than I expected". neglected_health fails in the opposite direction from usual — health is not the neglected corner of his life, it is the most attended one: "it's one of my priorities, and it should be everyone's priority to take care of your body. I would feel stupid not to do it." So the criteria pull against each other: the man the programme would most obviously benefit is the man least able to buy it, and the call ended in a $200-a-month downsell rather than a sale. Judged on outcomes this looks like a wasted hour; judged on fit it is evidence that the ICP is screening for wallet and calling it fit. Worth noting again that the criterion which should have gated this call — an unassessed acute back injury — appears nowhere in the ICP.
